newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas firms on weather, storage refills.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas firms on weather, storage refills.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were slightly higher Monday as cooler-than-expected weather arrived in parts of Texas and storage buying continued at a steady pace, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast swing gas prices rose another cent to the high-$1.90s, with Transco (Station 65) quoted at $2.00-2.05 and Henry Hub up about two cents at $1.98-2.00 per mmBtu.
Prices in south Texas were also marginally stronger in the low-to-mid $1.90s as slightly below-normal temperatures continued throughout most of the state.
At the New York city-gate, deals were reported done in the high-$2.30s to low-$2.40s, steady to higher from Friday's levels.
Appalachian prices climbed an equal amount to about $2.20 on Columbia and mid-$2.20s on CNG.
In the Midcontinent, prices were flat to about one cent higher at $1.85-$1.87, with Demarcation quoted in the low-to-mid $1.90s.
Chicago city-gate prices were also talked steady at $2.10-2.13.
Further west, Permian basin prices gained about four cents to the mid-to-high $1.80s as western buyers re-emerged to refill storage inventories and cover energy supplies missing on the nuclear side.

Boosting demand early in the western markets was the scheduled outage at the 1,080 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 3 nuclear unit, which is expected to last about 75 days. Also, Pacific Gas and Electric's 1,087 MW Diablo 2 nuclear unit was operating at 90 percent power and increasing early Monday following a weekend outage.
Southern California border prices were similarly higher in the mid-to-high $1.90s.
